EZ-Fin User Guide

How to set up EZ-Fin, use every screen, and get more from your household money. Tap any picture to enlarge it.

Welcome to EZ-Fin

EZ-Fin shows your household where your money goes, in about 30 minutes a month. You bring in your bank statements, give each line a category, and the app builds your dashboard, budget, reports and tax summary.

Everything rests on one simple sum, which you will see at the top of the Dashboard:

Gross income − Deductions = Net income − Expenses − Debt repayments = Cash flow

The screenshots in this guide use a made-up household, Thandi and Sipho. All names and amounts are fictional.

The five transaction types

Every line in EZ-Fin is one of five types. Pick the right one and your figures take care of themselves.

Type

What it means

Examples

Counts in your cash flow?

Income

Money you earned, before anything is taken off

Salary, side hustle, interest

Yes, adds

Deduction

Taken off your payslip before you are paid

PAYE tax, UIF, pension, medical aid

Yes, subtracts

Expense

Money spent

Groceries, fuel, school fees, loan interest

Yes, subtracts

Debt Repayment

The capital you pay off a loan

Home loan, vehicle finance

Yes, subtracts

Transfer

Your own money moving between your accounts

Credit card payment, ATM withdrawal, tax-free saving

No

An allocation is the category inside a type, such as Groceries & Cleaning or Fuel.

Getting started

You can be set up in about 20 minutes. Your first 30 days are free and no card is needed.

Create your account

  1. Go to app.ez-fin.co.za in your browser.
  2. Click the green Sign up – start your free trial button.
  3. Fill in your name, email and a password of at least 8 characters.
  4. Tick the Privacy Policy box, then click Create my account.
  5. If you are asked to confirm your email, click the link in the email and then log in.

Were you invited by someone already using EZ-Fin? Sign up with the same email address they added and you will join their account automatically.

Your first-time setup checklist

Work through these in order. Tick each one off as you go.

The one decision that matters: your credit card and cash

This is how EZ-Fin avoids counting the same money twice. The groceries you put on your card are spending. The payment you later make to the card is not new spending, because it only settles those groceries.

Do you record it in EZ-Fin?

Credit card

Cash

Yes (recommended)

You import the card statement. Purchases are Expenses and the card payment is a Transfer.

You capture cash slips. Slips are Expenses and ATM withdrawals are Transfers into Cash.

No

You skip the card statement. The card payment stays an Expense, so the spending is still counted.

You don't capture slips. ATM withdrawals count as an Expense called Cash spending.

Our suggestion: choose Yes for your credit card. You will see exactly what you bought, not just one large payment. Choose Yes for cash only if you will keep up with your slips.

Screen by screen

The tabs along the top take you to each screen. Numbered circles on the pictures match the numbered lists below them.

Dashboard

The Dashboard answers one question: is more coming in than going out?

  1. Year picker. Every screen shows the financial year chosen here.
  2. Filters. Narrow the view by allocation, account, person or month. Click Clear filters to reset.
  3. The money sum. Your figures from gross income down to cash flow.
  4. Money moved. Your own money moving around. Each box says whether it counts as spending.
  5. Save status. Cloud synced means your work is safely saved online.

Scroll down for the charts.

How to read it

  • Monthly breakdown: look for months where the red and purple bars rise close to the green bar.
  • Expenses by category: your top 10. The biggest bars are where a saving makes a real difference.
  • Net by person: what each person contributes after their own costs. A shared bill counts against whoever it was allocated to.

Suggestion: pick the current month in the Month filter on payday. That is your clearest view of how the month went.

Transactions

This is the full record of your money. Most lines arrive here from a statement import, but you can add any line by hand.

  1. New transaction. Add a line by hand.
  2. Cash slip. Photograph a till slip.
  3. Archive. See lines you have deleted, and restore them.
  4. Search and filters. Find anything by description, notes or allocation.
  5. Edit ticked / Delete ticked. Change or remove many lines at once.
  6. Tick boxes. Tick the lines you want to edit or delete.

Add an expense

  1. Click ＋ New transaction. Expense is already selected.
  2. Choose the date, type the amount and add a short description.
  3. Choose the Allocation, Paid from account and Person.
  4. Click Save transaction.

Got money back from a shop? Add it as an Expense in the same allocation and tick This is a refund. It reduces that category instead of counting as income.

Add a payslip

Click Income and the form changes to a payslip. Type each amount once, and EZ-Fin saves the income and every deduction as separate lines. The summary shows your take-home pay, which should match the amount paid into your bank.

Why capture the full payslip? Your bank statement only shows your take-home pay, but the Tax page needs your gross pay and PAYE. Important: when your statement is imported, remove the salary deposit from the Import Statement page. EZ-Fin cannot match it to your payslip because the amounts differ, so keeping it would count your salary twice.

Add a loan repayment

Click Debt. Type the full repayment, then type the interest in Interest included if you know it. EZ-Fin splits the two: capital becomes a Debt Repayment and interest becomes an Expense called Loan interest. Your loan statement shows the interest figure.

Add a transfer

Click Transfer, then choose the From account and To account. A transfer does not change your cash flow, so use it only for your own accounts. Money sent to anyone else is an Expense.

Fix or remove a line

  • To change one line: click Edit at the end of its row.
  • To change many lines: tick them, click ✏ Edit ticked, and set only the fields you want to change.
  • To delete: tick the lines, click 🗑 Delete ticked, type a reason and click Archive.

Deleted lines wait in the 🗄 Archive. Restore puts a line back. Delete there removes it for good.

Import Statement

This is the biggest time-saver in EZ-Fin. Imported lines wait here for your check, and nothing reaches your figures until you move it.

First, download your statement from your bank's online banking. CSV or Excel files give the most reliable result. PDF also works, but check those lines more carefully.

  1. Import statement. Choose CSV, Excel or PDF, then pick your file.
  2. Summary boxes. How many lines are waiting, need a category, are ready, or may be duplicates.
  3. Suggested. EZ-Fin has filled this in from your past lines or its own rules. Check that it is right.
  4. Red box. This line still needs an allocation.
  5. Yes tick. Tick this when the line is correct.
  6. Move ticked to Transactions. Sends the ticked lines to your records.

Import a statement step by step

  1. Go to Import Statement and click 📥 Import statement ▾.
  2. Choose your file type, then choose the file you downloaded.
  3. First time with this bank: the Match your statement columns window opens. See below.
  4. Next time: EZ-Fin remembers your layout and only asks which account the statement is for.
  5. Set Show to Needs allocation and choose an allocation for each red line.
  6. Set Show back to All and check the Suggested lines.
  7. Check any line with a warning tag. The table below explains each one.
  8. Click ✔ Tick all as ready, or tick Yes one line at a time.
  9. Click ➜ Move ticked to Transactions.

Matching your columns (first import only)

  1. Choose which account the statement is for.
  2. Check that Date and Description point to the right columns.
  3. Choose either one Amount column or separate Money in and Money out columns, whichever your bank uses.
  4. Check the preview. If money in and money out look reversed, tick Swap money in and money out.
  5. Leave Save this layout as ticked and type a name, such as your bank's name.
  6. Click Send to Import Statement.

Three handy tips

  • Change many lines at once: tick the box at the far left of each line, then click ✏ Edit selected.
  • Add a new category on the spot: choose ＋ New allocation… from the allocation dropdown.
  • Remove what doesn't belong: tick the line, then click 🗑 Remove selected. Your salary deposit is the common one if you capture payslips.

The more you import, the more EZ-Fin recognises. Your first statement takes the longest, and later ones get faster.

Capturing a cash slip

Photograph a till slip on your phone and EZ-Fin reads the shop, date and total for you.

  1. On Transactions, tap 📷 Cash slip.
  2. The first time, agree to use a Cash account. This stops your cash being counted twice.
  3. Tap Take a photo or Choose a picture.
  4. Wait while the slip is read. The first time takes longer, and you need internet access.
  5. Check the date, total and shop against the slip. Faded slips can be misread, and a total that can't be read stays blank for you to type.
  6. Choose an allocation. Use ＋ Split into another allocation if the slip covers more than one category.
  7. Tap Save slip.

Your photo is read on your own device. It is never uploaded or saved. Only the details you save are kept, so hold on to any slip you may need for a tax claim or warranty.

Budget

The Budget is your plan for the financial year, from March to February, category by category.

  1. Go to Budget.
  2. Click a cell and type the planned amount for that category and month.
  3. Repeat for each category. Your work saves as you type.

Reading the three boxes

  • Budgeted net / year: the cash flow your plan expects.
  • Actual net / year: your real cash flow so far.
  • Variance: actual minus budgeted.

Please note: if you budget all 12 months, Budgeted net covers the full year while Actual covers only the months so far. Variance is therefore most meaningful at year-end. During the year, compare your plan with the monthly figures in Reports.

Suggestions

  • Start with last month's real spending, then adjust. Reports shows you those figures.
  • Budget for once-a-year costs too, such as car licences, school uniforms and December.
  • Include your savings under Transfers and savings. These lines help you plan, but they are not in the totals.

Reports

Reports shows every category by month for the whole year, which makes it the best screen for spotting trends. Choose one person from the dropdown or leave it on All.

At the bottom, the Year-on-year summary compares your saved years and shows your savings rate.

Savings rate here means cash flow divided by net income. Money you moved to a tax-free account is still inside cash flow, because a transfer does not reduce it. Retirement annuity payments count as Expenses, so they are not included.

Click 🖨️ Print / PDF to print the report or save it as a PDF. It is useful to bring to a meeting with your bank or financial adviser.

Tax

The Tax page gathers what you need for your return, for the tax year from 1 March to the end of February. Choose one person at a time, because each person files their own return.

  • Taxable income (gross): all Income for that person. Check it against your IRP5, since some income may be taxed differently.
  • Total tax paid: deductions with Tax or PAYE in the allocation name.
  • Total claimable: the items you marked in Setup, multiplied by their claim %.

Set up your claimable items

  1. Go to Setup, then Tax-claimable allocations.
  2. Tick the items that apply, such as Retirement Annuity and Medical expenses.
  3. Type a claim % if only part applies, such as a home office share.

Please check these starting ticks. New accounts begin with every deduction ticked at 100%, including Tax, UIF and SDL. Tax is already shown under Total tax paid, and UIF and SDL are not items you claim. We suggest unticking those three so your total stays realistic. Medical aid works through a monthly tax credit rather than a deduction, so its "claimable" amount is a reminder, not a figure to enter.

The Tax page is a preparation aid. It does not calculate what you owe or replace your IRP5 or SARS's own figures.

Years

EZ-Fin works in financial years from 1 March to the end of February, matching the South African tax year.

  • Start a new year: click ＋ Start and agree to copy your budget across if you wish.
  • Two years at once: up to 2 can be open, so you can finish last year while starting the new one.
  • Switch years: click Switch to, or use the year picker at the top.
  • Save a copy: click CSV to download that year's transactions.

Closing a year locks it for good. Nothing can be added, changed or deleted afterwards, although you can still view it. EZ-Fin asks you to type the year to confirm.

EZ-Fin keeps 5 closed years. Closing a sixth removes the oldest, and a CSV copy downloads first. Keep that file.

Suggestion: don't rush to close. Wait until your tax return is filed and late bank charges and interest have come through.

Setup

Setup holds the lists used across the app.

  • Allocations: type in the box and click Add, or click × to remove one. Keep the list short, because too many categories slow you down.
  • Accounts and People: up to 10 accounts and 3 people.
  • Default person: the name filled in on new transactions.
  • Currency: the symbol shown across the app. It does not convert amounts.
  • Saved statement layouts: your bank formats. Remove one here if your bank changes its layout.

Take care with the Data box at the bottom of Setup. ↺ Reload sample data replaces your data with sample data, and Delete everything wipes it. Don't use either once you have real data in EZ-Fin.

Your account and plan

Click 👤 Account at the top to see your plan, renewal date and users.

  • Paying: click Pay monthly or Pay annually, and pay by card on iKhokha's secure page. EZ-Fin never sees your card number.
  • Payments are manual: you pay each period yourself, and nothing is debited automatically. The account owner gets email reminders first.
  • After your trial: you get 10 days of view-only access, then the account is suspended until you choose a plan.
  • After a missed renewal: you keep full access for 10 days, with a warning, before the account is suspended.
  • Adding a user: the account owner types their email under Users, then asks them to sign up with that same email. Up to 3 people share the same data.

Handy extras

  • Use it anywhere: log in from any browser on your computer, tablet or phone. Your data follows you.
  • Dark mode: click the 🌙 button at the top right.
  • Print: the Dashboard, Budget, Reports and Tax screens each have a print button.
  • Export: click 📤 Export CSV on Transactions to get a copy of your lines for Excel.
  • Log out: click ⚙️ Settings, then Log out. Do this on any shared computer.

Suggested routines

A small routine keeps EZ-Fin accurate. Thirty minutes a month is enough for most households.

Every week (5 minutes, optional)

Every month, just after payday (30 minutes)

Every year, from March

Recommendations for getting more from your money

The app gives you the numbers, and these five checks show what to do with them. Do them once a quarter. The examples use Thandi and Sipho's 8 months of figures, and the targets are common rules of thumb, not personal advice.

Check

How to work it out

Example

Rule of thumb

Savings rate

Cash flow ÷ Net income

R32 854 ÷ R376 823 = 8.7%

Work towards 10% to 20%

Debt load

(Debt repayments + Loan interest) ÷ Gross income

R135 200 ÷ R504 000 = 26.8%

Lower is safer, and watch the trend

Monthly cost of living

(Expenses + Debt repayments) ÷ months so far

R343 969 ÷ 8 = R42 996

Use this for the next check

Emergency fund

Monthly cost of living × 3 to 6

R128 988 to R257 977

Keep it in an easy-to-reach account

Cost of borrowing

Find Loan interest on the Dashboard

R73 200, the largest expense

Paying extra capital reduces this

Make the most of your spending

  • Start with the three biggest bars under Expenses by category. A 10% cut there beats cancelling small treats.
  • Check Subscriptions and Bank Fees yearly. They are small, regular and easy to forget.
  • Clear expensive debt first. Credit card and personal loan interest usually costs more than savings earn.
  • Keep Miscellaneous small. If it grows, your picture of where money goes gets blurry.

Make the most of tax

Figures below were checked on 2 November 2026 and can change each Budget.

  • Tax-free savings: you can put in up to R46 000 a tax year and R500 000 in your lifetime. That is about R3 833 a month. Going over the limit costs 40% of the excess. Use the Tax free savings box on your Dashboard to track it.
  • Retirement contributions: these are deductible up to 27.5% of the greater of remuneration or taxable income, capped at R430 000 a year. Tick Retirement Annuity in Setup so it shows on the Tax page.
  • Medical credits: the 2027 year of assessment gives R376 a month for you, R752 with one dependant, and R254 for each extra dependant. Record medical costs you pay yourself under Medical expenses.
  • Records: SARS expects you to keep supporting documents for 5 years from submitting your return. EZ-Fin keeps your figures, but not your slips or certificates, so file those separately.

Keep your data trustworthy

  • Allocate consistently. Fuel should always be Fuel, so your trends stay meaningful.
  • Import every account. One missing statement makes your cash flow look better than it is.
  • Use Notes for anything you may need to explain later, such as a claim or a once-off cost.
  • Share with your household. Up to 3 people can log in, and decisions stick when everyone sees the same numbers.

EZ-Fin is a record-keeping and planning tool. It does not provide financial or tax advice, so speak to a registered financial adviser or tax practitioner about your situation.

Common questions

Is my information safe? Connections and stored data are encrypted. Your finance data is visible only to the users on your account, and EZ-Fin administrators cannot open it. Bank account numbers are shortened to the last 4 digits. Read the full Privacy Policy.

Does EZ-Fin connect to my bank? No. You download your statement and import it, so EZ-Fin never needs your banking login.

Can I work without internet? Briefly. If you've logged in recently, EZ-Fin keeps working for up to 5 days and syncs when you reconnect.

What happens to my data if I stop paying? It is kept for 12 months so you can come back, and is then permanently deleted. You can ask for it to be deleted sooner.

Can I start part-way through the year? Yes. Start with your latest statement, then work back to 1 March if you want a full tax year.

What if I make a mistake? Edit the line, or delete it and restore it from the Archive if needed. Only a closed year can't be changed.
